caption:
Three steps in one workflow. Only one of them is worth automating.

Step 1: read the brief.
Step 2: copy the same client details into three different tools.
Step 3: decide the price.

Most people reach for step 3 first, because it feels like the expensive one. It isn't. Step 3 is judgment — it changes with every client, and it is where the work is actually worth something.

Step 2 is the one to hand over. It is identical every time, it produces nothing new, and a mistake in it costs more than the time it takes.

The test is simple: if you could write down the exact rule for doing it, and the rule never changes, it can be automated. If the rule starts with "it depends", keep it.

Which step in your week is the copy-paste one? Tell me in the comments.
